Primary Purpose: Everyday general-purpose computing (browsing, office tasks, media consumption)
Key Features: Traditional clamshell design, standard 14-15.6 inch screen, full keyboard, standard port selection
Performance & Portability: Balanced mid-range performance; moderate weight and battery life

Primary Purpose: High-end video gaming, 3D rendering, and GPU-intensive tasks
Key Features: High-refresh-rate display (120Hz+), dedicated discrete GPU (NVIDIA RTX / AMD Radeon), aggressive cooling, RGB lighting
Performance & Portability: High power consumption, bulky and heavy chassis, shorter battery life

Primary Purpose: Premium productivity on the go for professionals and students
Key Features: Ultra-slim profile, lightweight build, premium metal chassis (aluminum/magnesium), fast SSD storage, all-day battery life
Performance & Portability: High power efficiency; typically relies on integrated graphics or low-power dedicated GPUs

Primary Purpose: Versatile work and creative input (digital note-taking, sketching, presentations)
Key Features: 360-degree hinge or detachable screen; touchscreen with active stylus pen support; transitions between laptop, tent, and tablet modes
Performance & Portability: Similar performance and battery life to Ultrabooks, with added touchscreen and hinge versatility

Primary Purpose: Heavy professional and computational workloads (CAD, 3D animation, data science, video rendering)
Key Features: ISV-certified components, professional-grade GPUs (e.g., NVIDIA RTX A-series / Ada Generation), support for ECC RAM, maximum thermal headroom
Performance & Portability: Extreme processing power and reliability; bulky, heavy, and higher price point

Primary Purpose: Ultra-light web browsing, email, and basic text editing
Key Features: Very small form factor (typically 10-12 inches), highly portable, budget-friendly
Performance & Portability: Low-power entry-level processors (e.g., Intel Celeron/Atom); limited RAM and storage capacity
